title: One Missing, One Repeated

concept.title: Compare what is there with what should be there
body: The numbers `1, 2, ..., n` should each appear exactly once. Here one of them appears twice and another one is missing. Count how often each value occurs, then walk over the values `1..n`: the one with count 2 is the repeated number and the one with count 0 is the missing number.
This works for any "should be there" check: build the counts from the data, then ask the map about every expected value.

statement: An array has `n` integers, each between 1 and `n`. Exactly one value occurs twice and exactly one value of `1..n` does not occur at all; every other value occurs once. Print the repeated value and the missing value.
outputFormat: Print the repeated value and the missing value separated by a space.
hints: Count the occurrences of every value.
Look at the values 1 to n: a count of 2 is the repeated one, a count of 0 is the missing one.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: After counting, the expected values `1..n` are checked one by one: count 2 marks the repeated number and count 0 the missing one.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).
